taxonomy.note: Accepted species; Texas-native at state level but target-zone range fails.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Ilex opaca and lists Texas within its native range at the state level.
USDA PLANTS-derived county data records 38 native Texas counties, but none are in the project's current target-zone county list.
The Texas county layer is concentrated in eastern/southeastern Texas, including Anderson, Angelina, Brazos, Cherokee, Harris, Nacogdoches, Polk, Walker, Wood and others.
NPSOT likewise maps American holly to East Central Texas Plains, Gulf Coast Prairies/Marshes, and Western Gulf Coastal Plain rather than the project's core Central/West target counties.
The user's one wild iNaturalist observation is encounter evidence only and cannot override the county-native range layer.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Texas-native at the state level does not satisfy the project's target-zone rule. Do not count planted American hollies or a single iNaturalist observation as proof of Central Texas nativity.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the leaf immediately: American holly is the big-leaved evergreen tree, with thick dark-green leaves bearing prominent stiff spine-tipped teeth—dramatically larger and sharper than yaupon foliage.
diagnostic_traits: evergreen tree, commonly with a pyramidal crown when young
leaves alternate, simple, thick and leathery, substantially larger than yaupon leaves
leaf margins often armed with several sharp stiff spine-tipped teeth; upper-canopy leaves can be less spiny
leaf upper surface dark glossy green, lower surface paler
small pale greenish-white unisexual flowers; species is dioecious
female trees produce bright red drupes that persist into winter
gray bark becomes rougher with age
native Texas distribution is principally eastern and southeastern

confusers.separator: Yaupon has tiny evergreen leaves with low crenate teeth; American holly has much larger, thicker leaves with stiff spines.
Possumhaw is deciduous with thinner, non-spiny leaves and bare fruiting twigs in winter; American holly remains leafy and evergreen.
Chinese holly is a common introduced ornamental with strongly horned/spiny leaves; landscape plants should be separated using leaf shape, fruiting, provenance, and horticultural context.

learner_role.reason: Texas-native but outside the project's strict 3-county target-zone rule; useful evergreen holly comparison and common landscape encounter. Requires explicit approval for comparison retention.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native. May be retained only if Calvin explicitly approves its labeled comparison role; exclude from native totals.
